title: Perceptron

paper.title: The Perceptron: A Probabilistic Model for Information Storage and Organization in the Brain
paper.year_note: Original/preprint year except GCN (2017 venue, 2016 preprint) and speculative decoding (2023 venue, 2022 preprint).

statement: Implement Perceptron: fit separable blobs with the online mistake-driven linear update. Read the linked paper and isolate the named mechanism. Write a self-contained solve(data), fit using training tensors only, and return Submission(model=model). Keep validation labels out of fitting and preprocessing. This is an educational reduced-scale adaptation, not a claim to reproduce original paper results. Use blobs; required output: [N,D] -> [N,C] logits. Evaluate accuracy (maximize). Online mistake updates; no autograd required. Required ablation: Compare raw and averaged iterates with identical example order.

dataset.description: Online mistake updates; no autograd required
dataset.split_policy: Disjoint train/validation/test examples; fit preprocessing using training data only.

checks: Return a Submission containing a torch module.
